newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Qantas cuts further 132 engineering jobs.
newsitem.headline: Qantas cuts further 132 engineering jobs.

text.p: Qantas Airways Ltd said on Tuesday that it would retrench 132 staff from its engineering and maintenance division.
In a statement, chief executive James Strong said the staff reductions were unavoidable for Qantas to remain viable and improve productivity and efficiency.
"Continuing reviews of our business efficiencies have identified the need and the potential to reduce staff in most areas of the company," he said.
Counting 53 apprentices laid off last week, the latest cuts bring the total number of jobs lost in the division to 185.
Strong said such redundancies were inevitable in the airline industry because it faced more competition with the liberalisation of markets and attendant pricing pressures.

"This is in line with the approach of virtually all airlines around the world who are seeking to improve efficiency and to reduce costs, due to the continual decline in the real level of airfares over recent years," he said.
Qantas is 25 percent owned by British Airways Plc.
Qantas shares closed five cents higher at A$2.70 on turnover of 1.5 million shares.
